rule: Lazy instanced dungeon. (1) Start room exits each lead to an instance; a 5-minute ticker gives each start exit a 50 percent chance of reset, so the next party through gets a fresh instance, while a party using the same exit within the window shares it. (2) Stepping through an unbuilt exit creates a branch (one per instance) and builds the first room. (3) Build a room: target = current coordinates plus direction shift; depth = int(sqrt(x*x + y*y)); name and text from a depth table (10 entries, then dark fallback); always add an unlocked return exit. (4) Frontier budget: if fewer than two unvisited exits, add one or two new exits in shuffled directions to coordinates not yet in the grid or the start; reserve each target with an empty value until built. (5) Forward exits are locked while the room carries a not-clear tag; clear removes the tag. (6) Branch stamp refreshed only on build; hourly deleter collapses branches stamped more than a week ago, moving tagged characters to the start room with a collapse message (room cleanup is broken, see defects).

look_test: In a test zone build one instance: entrance with two start exits, a six-room branch with a two-exit frontier, and one locked room that clears on a test kill. Dom plays it in a 375-wide text panel for about two minutes. Pass: each new room's name matches its depth; the blocked footer shows until the test kill; with life set to two minutes for the test, a forced collapse returns him to the entrance with the collapse line. Dom answers: did the walk feel like it led somewhere; did the blocked line make him stop and fight.
